decisions.executionNote: Begin left-tube approach with open gripper, raising and rotating gradually to preserve elbow-up continuity.
Advance above the left tube while pitching toward a downward side grasp; adjust yaw to the visible tube axis.
Lower and center the left gripper on the tube body; use small orientation corrections before closing.
Visually refine the grasp along the tube toward its cap and center it between the fingers before closing.
Close around the left tube body, then make a short lift to check visual retention.
Tube appears retained. Lift clear of the tabletop and begin a gradual upright rotation toward the left rack slot.
Transport the retained tube toward the rack while continuing the upright rotation in small increments.
Finish bringing the tube upright above a left-side rack opening; keep it elevated for alignment.
Refine left-slot alignment from the camera and lower partway, keeping the tube upright and closed.
Small lateral correction toward the left-front opening, then slow vertical insertion while retaining the tube.
The tube appears supported at the rack; open and withdraw gently to verify that it remains upright in the opening.
Withdraw the left arm toward home while beginning the right-arm approach to the nearer right tube, preserving elbow-up motion.
Continue the right approach above the nearer tube, aligning the downward gripper with its axis; keep the left arm retracting safely.
Finish returning the left arm and lower the open right gripper around the nearer tube, completing axis alignment.
Refine the nearer right tube's yaw alignment, close on its body, and start a minimal lift to check retention.
Lift the retained right tube clear of the table, then begin rotating it upright without changing arm configuration.
Carry the second tube toward a right-side rack opening while progressively rotating it upright.
Continue the elevated transport and upright rotation, keeping the second tube retained.
Finish the upright orientation above the right rack area, then inspect the slot alignment before descending.
Align the second tube with the right-front opening and descend partway, checking rack clearance.
Lower the upright second tube slowly into the aligned right opening; maintain the grasp until seating is checked.
The second tube appears supported in the rack. Open the gripper and withdraw to check that it stays upright.
The second tube may be resting near the rim rather than fully seated; return the open gripper for a small alignment correction.
Regrasp and lift the second tube slightly to clear the rim before shifting toward the visible large opening.
Make a small centering adjustment over the right-front opening and lower the tube back to seating depth.
Release the supported second tube and move the open gripper clear to inspect its seating.
The second tube tipped after release. Clear the gripper and inspect its settled position before recovery.
Begin a gradual, elevated reorientation for recovering the tipped tube; watch for IK continuity limits.
Continue the elevated recovery approach, rotating gradually while keeping clear of the rack.
Continue the slow recovery reorientation above the fallen tube, maintaining clearance and joint continuity.
Bring the open right gripper above the fallen tube body while completing the downward approach gradually.
Refine the recovery gripper orientation to the fallen tube axis and approach its body from above.
Back away from the wrist wrap boundary, then improve the downward approach without continuing the rejected yaw change.
Center over the fallen tube body, straighten the downward approach, and lower cautiously with the gripper open.
Close on the recovered tube body and lift a short distance to check that it is retained.
The recovered tube is visibly retained. Lift it clear before reversing the wrist reorientation for another insertion.
Reverse the recovery wrist rotation gradually, keeping the retained tube elevated and unwinding away from the joint limit.
Continue unwinding toward upright while moving slightly away from the rack for clearance.
Keep unwinding the wrist and bring the retained tube toward an interior rack opening, remaining above the rack.
Finish bringing the recovered tube upright above an interior opening, then inspect its alignment before insertion.
Straighten the recovered tube and align it with a central large opening while lowering to just above the rack.
Lower the centered tube into the interior opening with a small frontward correction; retain it while checking depth.
Continue the slow insertion to the estimated seated depth, then pause before releasing.
The tube appears supported at depth. Open gradually, pause, and withdraw slightly to check whether it remains upright.
The tube tipped again. Clear the open gripper to locate its settled position and correct the rack-depth estimate.
Raise clear and reorient for another recovery; the next placement must be farther into the rack rather than at its front edge.
Approach the fallen tube from above, using a recovery orientation with margin from the wrist wrap limit.
Continue the elevated recovery approach toward the tube midpoint with small, continuous wrist increments.
Continue rotating down above the fallen tube and approach its body slowly, keeping wrist-wrap margin.
Refine the downward recovery pose and center over the tube while leaving margin from the wrist wrap boundary.
Close around the recovered tube and make a short retention-check lift before transporting again.
